Question Choices: What constant relates consecutive terms of an arithmetic sequence?
Hints: Subtract one term from the next.|The same amount is added each time.
Solution: An arithmetic sequence adds the same signed difference d each time. From the first to the nth term there are n-1 steps, so a_n=a_1+(n-1)d. A recursive rule can be iterated or converted to this formula. It is the common difference d.

Question Choices: Write the arithmetic-series sum formula using the first term a1 and last term an.
Hints: Average the first and last terms.|Multiply by the number of terms.
Solution: For n>=1 arithmetic terms, write the sum forward and backward. Adding corresponding terms gives n copies of a_1+a_n, so 2S_n=n(a_1+a_n), hence S_n=n(a_1+a_n)/2. This proof works for odd or even n. For 1+...+n each forward/reverse pair totals n+1. S_n = n(a1 + an)/2.
